    # Slugify a filename or title into a URL-safe fragment.
    #
    # See Jekyll::Utils.slugify for the supported modes and examples.
    def self.slugify(string, mode: nil, cased: false)
      return nil if string.nil?

      new(
        :template     => string,
        :placeholders => { :mode => mode, :cased => cased }
      ).slugify

    def slugify
      string = @template
      mode = @placeholders[:mode] || @placeholders["mode"]
      cased = @placeholders[:cased]
      cased = @placeholders["cased"] if cased.nil?
      mode ||= "default"
      cased = false if cased.nil?

      unless Utils::SLUGIFY_MODES.include?(mode)
        return cased ? string : string.downcase
      end

      # Drop accent marks from latin characters. Everything else turns to ?
      if mode == "latin"
        i18n_config = I18n.config
        if i18n_config.available_locales.empty?
          i18n_config.available_locales = :en
        end
        string = I18n.transliterate(string)
      end

      replaceable_char =
        case mode
        when "raw"
          Utils::SLUGIFY_RAW_REGEXP
        when "pretty"
          # "._~!$&'()+,;=@" is human readable (not URI-escaped) in URL
          # and is allowed in both extN and NTFS.
          Utils::SLUGIFY_PRETTY_REGEXP
        when "ascii"
          # For web servers not being able to handle Unicode, the safe
          # method is to ditch anything else but latin letters and numeric
          # digits.
          Utils::SLUGIFY_ASCII_REGEXP
        else
          Utils::SLUGIFY_DEFAULT_REGEXP
        end

      # Strip according to the mode
      slug = string.gsub(replaceable_char, "-")

      # Remove leading/trailing hyphen
      slug.gsub!(%r!^\-|\-$!i, "")

      slug.downcase! unless cased

      if slug.empty?
        logger = Jekyll.logger
        adapter_level = logger.level
        writer = logger.writer
        if LogAdapter::LOG_LEVELS.fetch(adapter_level) <= LogAdapter::LOG_LEVELS.fetch(:warn)
          writer_level = writer.level
          if writer_level.nil? || writer_level <= LogAdapter::LOG_LEVELS.fetch(:warn)
            logger.warn("Warning:", "Empty `slug` generated for '#{string}'.")

part.text:
Fixed. The change in `lib/jekyll/utils.rb:16-17` replaces the POSIX `[:alnum:]` character class with Unicode category classes in the slugify regexes:

```ruby
SLUGIFY_DEFAULT_REGEXP = Regexp.new("[^\\p{M}\\p{L}\\p{Nd}]+").freeze
SLUGIFY_PRETTY_REGEXP = Regexp.new("[^\\p{M}\\p{L}\\p{Nd}._~!$&'()+,;=@]+").freeze
```

This preserves Unicode marks (`\p{M}`), letters (`\p{L}`), and decimal digits (`\p{Nd}`) instead of only `alnum`, so `மல்லிப்பூ வகைகள்` now slugifies to `மல்லிப்பூ-வகைகள்` in both `default` and `pretty` modes.

Verification:
- The previously-failing test (`TestUtils: should not replace Unicode 'Mark', 'Letter', or 'Number: Decimal Digit' category characters`) now passes, as do all 22 slugify tests in `test_url.rb`/`test_utils.rb`.
- Full suite comparison before vs. after shows the only remaining failure is a pre-existing, unrelated rouge-highlighter test; the ~115 `ExecJS::RuntimeUnavailable` errors occur identically on the pristine tree (missing JS runtime in the container).
